criteria.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has a new entry listing ten test binaries, slowest first, each with its 'finished in' seconds, and naming the GitHub run id (newest green main run) they came from.
criteria.evidence: The only change is a 6-line CHANGELOG.md entry saying the ten slowest binaries 'could not be listed' because `gh` was not available. It lists no binaries, no times and no run id.

criteria.criterion: The CHANGELOG entry states the slowest binary's local time before and after the change, from running only that binary, or states that the cause cannot be fixed without losing coverage and no code changed.
criteria.evidence: The entry gives no before or after time. It also does not say the cause cannot be fixed without losing coverage. It says the CI logs could not be reached, so the slowest binary was never found. The request allows a no-code outcome only when a fix would lose coverage, not when the job could not get its input.

criteria.criterion: The diff touches test code of only the single slowest binary (plus CHANGELOG.md); no other test binary is modified.
criteria.evidence: Only CHANGELOG.md changed and no test binary was modified, so this is met, but only because nothing was done.

criteria.criterion: Every test function present in the changed binary before the change still exists afterwards with equivalent assertions (git diff shows no removed #[test] without a replacement and no weakened assertions).
criteria.evidence: No test file changed, so no test was removed or weakened. Met only because nothing was done.

criteria.criterion: Run cargo test on only the changed binary (cargo test -p <package> --test <name>); it passes, and its reported 'finished in' time is below the 'before' time stated in CHANGELOG.md.
criteria.evidence: No binary changed and CHANGELOG.md states no 'before' time, so there was nothing to run or compare. No speedup is shown.

findings.summary: Behavior criterion 5 is unmet: its evidence must cite commands that ran (D43)
The requested work was not done: no CI timings were read, no ten-slowest list was written and no binary was sped up.
findings.evidence: The diff adds only a note that `gh` was not available to the producer. The brief assumed the producer could read CI logs. If that tooling was missing, the producer should have reported the block in its output and left the repository unchanged. Instead it committed a status message as a changelog entry.

findings.summary: The CHANGELOG entry records a job failure rather than a change to the project.
findings.evidence: Under '### Changed' it says 'Slowest-test-binary speedup not done ... Rerun the job with access to the CI logs.' This is an instruction to the job runner. To a maintainer reading the changelog it describes no change to the project. It also wrongly treats 'no CI access' as the request's allowed no-code outcome, which applies only when a fix would cost coverage.

summary: This change fails. It adds only a CHANGELOG.md note saying the work could not be done because `gh` was not available, and it touches no code. It names no slowest test binaries, gives no CI run id or times, and speeds nothing up. Criteria 1, 2 and 5 are not met. Criteria 3 and 4 are met only because nothing changed. The changelog note is also a job-status message rather than a change to the project, so it should not be committed. To finish this, rerun the job with access to the GitHub Actions logs.
